planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Deliciosa is one of the long-documented California cherimoya selections best suited to zones 9b-11 and mild coastal microclimates further north. Hand-pollination is strongly recommended for consistent fruit set.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Deliciosa has been grown in California home orchards for generations and is one of the named cultivars long catalogued by California Rare Fruit Growers alongside Bays, Booth, and Whaley, giving it a track record in the state's cool coastal cherimoya districts. Fruit carries the classic custard apple combination of pineapple, banana, and vanilla notes in smooth, creamy white flesh once fully ripe and slightly soft to the touch. As with other cherimola selections, the flowers rarely self-pollinate reliably, so hand-transferring pollen from newly opened male-phase blossoms to receptive female-phase blossoms with a small brush in the morning markedly improves yield. Give young grafted trees frost protection for their first few winters and consistent moisture through fruit swell.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Spain is a historic California cherimoya cultivar suited to zones 9b-11, grown on introduced Iberian stock that proved adaptable to the state's Mediterranean-type coastal climate.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Spain is a longstanding named cherimoya selection documented in California cultivar lists alongside Deliciosa, Bays, and Whaley, tracing back to Iberian-origin planting stock that growers found well suited to the state's dry-summer coastal conditions. The fruit ripens to tender, custardy white flesh with the sweet, aromatic pineapple-banana-vanilla flavor typical of good cherimoya, best eaten once the skin yields slightly to gentle thumb pressure. Because cherimola flowers open as female first and male later, natural self-pollination is unreliable, so hand-pollinating with a small brush between trees in the morning is the single best way to raise fruit set in a home orchard. Protect young trees from frost and keep soil evenly moist while fruit is developing.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Bonita is one of the commercial cultivars grown on Spain's Costa Tropical of Granada and Málaga and performs best in zones 9-11 with mild winters and low humidity.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Bonita is among the named cultivars grown commercially on Spain's Costa Tropical of Granada and Málaga, the Mediterranean region recognized under the EU protected geographical indication for chirimoya, where it is planted alongside Fino de Jete and Campas. Fruit has a relatively smooth, lightly tuberculate skin and sweet, fine-textured white pulp with the characteristic custard apple blend of tropical fruit flavors. Growers in the region prize it as part of a cultivar mix that spreads the harvest window and diversifies fruit shape and skin texture for market. Hand pollination with a soft brush between morning-open male and female flowers remains the most reliable way to secure a full fruit set outside the tree's native Andean pollinator range.
sources: European Commission — Protected Geographical Indication, Chirimoya de la Costa Tropical de Granada-Málaga

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Campas is grown commercially on Spain's Costa Tropical of Granada and Málaga and is suited to zones 9-11 with mild, nearly frost-free winters.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Campas is a traditional Spanish cultivar grown on the Costa Tropical of Granada and Málaga, planted as part of the same regional cultivar mix as Fino de Jete and Bonita under Spain's protected geographical indication for chirimoya. The fruit is valued locally for its sweet, aromatic flesh and conical shape, ripening with the species' characteristic soft custard texture once the skin loses its hard green color and gives slightly to pressure. Because it flowers on a slightly different schedule than other cultivars in a mixed planting, growers sometimes use it to extend hand-pollination windows across an orchard block. Keep soil consistently moist through fruit set and swell, and shield young trees from the occasional cold snap in their first winters.
sources: European Commission — Protected Geographical Indication, Chirimoya de la Costa Tropical de Granada-Málaga

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Concha Lisa ('smooth shell') is grown commercially on Spain's Costa Tropical of Granada and Málaga and suits zones 9-11 with mild, dry winters.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Concha Lisa takes its Spanish name, meaning 'smooth shell,' from skin that lacks the pronounced bumpy, fingerprint-like markings typical of most cherimoya, giving the fruit a notably even, almost polished rind. It is one of the named cultivars grown on Spain's Costa Tropical of Granada and Málaga alongside Fino de Jete, Bonita, and Campas, prized by growers partly for how cleanly its smoother skin presents in the market. Inside, the flesh is the same sweet, fragrant white custard typical of good cherimoya, ready to eat once the fruit softens slightly and loses its hard green color. Hand pollination with a small brush between morning-open flowers remains the most dependable way to raise fruit set away from the species' native Andean pollinators.
sources: European Commission — Protected Geographical Indication, Chirimoya de la Costa Tropical de Granada-Málaga

planting.note: Plant grafted or container-grown trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Purandar is a Maharashtra-selected sugar apple suited to zones 10-11 and warm, sheltered zone 9b sites with no cold tolerance to speak of.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Purandar is a custard apple selection associated with Purandar taluka in Maharashtra's Pune district, one of India's most important sugar apple growing regions, and is grown there for its large, well-filled fruit and comparatively high yield under the region's dry, warm climate. The pale green, segmented fruit ripens to soft, sweet, custard-textured white flesh with the classic sugar apple flavor, and like other Annona squamosa selections it softens and the segments loosen slightly as it nears peak ripeness. It tolerates the drier conditions of the Deccan plateau better than more humidity-dependent Annona types, making it a practical choice for warm, semi-arid zone 10-11 gardens. Hand-pollination in the early morning or evening, when flowers are receptive, improves fruit set where the tree's natural beetle pollinators are scarce, and harvested fruit should be eaten promptly since it does not store well once ripe.
